name: Karl Okafor

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior researcher at the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI companies, unions, parties and government. This stays confidential. What did you spend most of yesterday doing?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: A hardware wholesaler had counted a returned drill twice, so I checked the stock book against the bank credit before I could finish its tax return. I'm 43 and a mid-level accountant at Pine Ledger, experienced and about average, with a bachelor's degree and a professional accountancy qualification. I like when a shop owner sees exactly why the margin changed; I dislike chasing the missing credit note at closing time.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What happens at home after a day like that, and where does AI fit?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Amira is a school librarian, and our children are nine and twelve; the younger one always wants me to look at a drawing before dinner. We have a mortgage, my pay is high for an accountant at my level, eight months of bills saved and plenty of similar firms nearby. I use AI now and then for a draft after a colleague has tested it, but I check each stock figure myself. My parents ran a small shop, and I still believe a business should earn its customers and a family should build its own cushion.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau — Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the shop owners a quicker stock search is useful if we still show them the credit note. I wouldn't charge for a tool that only makes an error look tidy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our two wages and eight months saved make the mortgage steady, and the hardware clients keep paying for careful accounts. I do not expect my hours to fall because of a small sorting tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep tracing returned stock to bank credits and use AI only for a letter I check myself. In the first year I'd add one hundred a month from pay to the household reserve and leave the children's lessons alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and the loan. A little quicker search could give me more time at dinner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the returned drill teach you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The supplier refunded the drill on Monday, but the shop recorded the return on Friday. I followed the credit note before changing the tax entry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy more software?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not before the firm shows it saves more than the checking it creates. I can learn a tool once another accountant has proved it on old files.

say: I would keep the **credit note** behind every returned-stock figure.
I would price the **actual checking time** before buying software.
think: Our **mortgage feels steady** with high pay and eight months saved.
I do not expect a **paid-hours cut** in a plateau.
do: Keep tracing **returned stock** to bank credits with current checks.
Save **one hundred monthly** from pay into the household reserve.
feel: He feels **calm** about work and mortgage payments.
S0.quote: I wouldn't charge for a tool that only makes an error look tidy.
fieldNote: He values a **visible credit note** and treats a small tool as a priced business choice.
Eight months saved and steady school-library pay make **family money secure** through mild automation.

steps.text: Keep tracing returned hardware stock to bank credits
Add one hundred monthly from pay into household reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption — Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to show which checks the new system passes and which ones it misses. If it cuts a paid day from the rota, they should say that directly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Most of my paid work is checking stock figures and writing tax explanations, so I could lose hours even if Pine Ledger keeps its clients. Eight months saved gives us time to find another post, but it would be hard to replace my high pay exactly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take a paid demonstration on ten closed hardware files with the senior if the firm agrees, then keep a list of wrong credit matches. In the first year of steady change, if my paid week falls below four days, I'd apply for posted accounts roles at the nearby firms while keeping Pine Ledger hours until a written wage and start date are agreed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing pay, not about learning one proven tool. The mortgage still expects the full monthly amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the paid demonstration is refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stay with the current stock checks and ask the partners for their hours plan. I would not send client figures into an unapproved tool from home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a new job need to offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A written salary that still covers the mortgage after travel, with a start time that lets Amira or me collect the younger child. I wouldn't resign for an advertisement alone.

I would demand a **clear paid-hours plan** from the partners.

do: Attend a **paid old-file demonstration** with senior review if approved.
Keep **current stock checks** if paid testing is refused.
Seek **posted nearby accounts** below four paid days with written mortgage-covering net wage/start and pickup; keep Pine Ledger hours until terms agreed.
feel: He feels **anxious** about reduced pay despite a useful cushion.
S1.quote: I wouldn't resign for an advertisement alone.
fieldNote: He will try a proven tool through **paid old-file work** and record missed credits.
His job move requires a **written mortgage-covering salary** and school-pickup hours; a refusal leaves current pay intact.

Keep paid Pine Ledger hours until written outside wage and start date are agreed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 — Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell clients full AGI in 2028 can do the thinking side of accounts, so the firm should be honest about the cost of a human review. The robots around 2031 do not give a tax desk three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Pine Ledger to cut some accounting posts when cheap AGI handles returns, and I may be one of them. Amira's school-library work may also change through AI, so even eight months saved would not make two lost wages easy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd add two hundred monthly from my current pay to our emergency fund and stop the planned larger-car purchase. In the first year after 2028, if my post ends, I'd apply for posted salaried stock-control roles at nearby hardware wholesalers and keep any paid Pine Ledger checks while waiting for a written offer with wage and start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a possible lost salary, but I can use savings and several employers before the mortgage is late. I cannot assume a posted job will come with my current pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for stock-control work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only with a signed offer that covers the loan and a new school pickup plan. I would not sell the house because a warehouse manager sounded interested.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no wholesaler is hiring?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask Pine Ledger for whatever paid return checks remain and keep the fund for bills. I won't put the reserve into a business nobody has paid for.

say: I would ask for a **priced human review** when AGI prepares returns.
I would separate **2028 desk risk** from later robots.
think: My **accounting post** may be cut when cheap AGI handles tax returns in 2028.
Amira’s **library work** may also change under thinking AI.
do: Save **two hundred monthly** from current pay.
Delay the **larger car** before spending the reserve.
Seek **posted hardware stock-control** after job loss, keeping paid Pine Ledger checks until written wage/start are agreed.
feel: He feels **anxious** about possible job loss with a search cushion.
S2.quote: I cannot assume a posted job will come with my current pay.
fieldNote: He keeps the larger-car money for **household liquidity** while adding new cash each month.
The wholesaler search needs a **real vacancy** and written pay, with firm checks kept meanwhile.

steps.text: Add two hundred monthly from pay to emergency fund
Apply for posted salaried hardware stock-control after job loss; require written wage/start and pickup plan
Keep available paid Pine Ledger checks while seeking written outside offer with wage and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031 — Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years lets the firm find out whether hardware shops still pay for advice on stock losses. I want signed client fees, not a job promise built on polite interest.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 48 in 2031 I would still have children in school and a mortgage. AGI could do the accounts work I sell, so even a year of savings would be a bridge rather than a career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask Pine Ledger to let me handle monthly paid stock-loss meetings with three existing shop clients, with the fees going to the firm. In the first year after 2031, if two clients renew at fees covering my salaried hours, I'd stay; otherwise I'd apply for posted salaried stock-control work and keep any funded returns until a written offer starts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though five years lets us test whether owners pay for an explanation. I cannot budget a polite thank you.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you bring to a meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd bring the list of missing drills, the returned-stock credits and a short note on where the margin went. If the owner refuses a second paid visit, the service has no wage behind it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your partners decline to fund meetings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing current accounts and ask for a written staffing plan. I would not use unpaid evenings to persuade them.

I would require **two renewals** covering salaried hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036 — Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years is time to reduce debt and see which shop owners will still pay for a person to explain a loss. I wouldn't put the family house behind an untested service.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 in 2036 the children may be older, but I would still need a wage. AGI reaches my desk then; robots around 2039 may reach the hardware shops, so the service might change too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pay an extra one hundred and fifty monthly off the mortgage while our two wages hold and track repeat fees from the shop meetings. In the first year after 2036, if the meetings still fund my salary, I'd stay; if not, I'd apply for posted paid accounts roles at nearby firms and keep current hours until a written wage and start date replace them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a job at 53, though the loan could be smaller. Ten years gives us room to plan, not permission to stop earning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if one wage falls before then?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stop the extra loan payment and keep the cash for food and mortgage bills. A smaller mortgage balance is no comfort if the next instalment cannot be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, eight months saved is a buffer, not a pension. I'd work while I can and help the children with school costs as long as wages allow.

I would watch **repeat shop fees** before relying on advice.
think: At **53 in 2036**, I still need income for our family and the remaining mortgage.
Robots around **2039** may change the hardware clients too.
do: Pay **one hundred fifty** extra monthly off mortgage while both wages hold.

Apply for **posted local accounting** if meetings cannot fund salary.

S4.quote: A smaller mortgage balance is no comfort if the next instalment cannot be paid.

The 2036 fallback requires **posted paid work** and a written start before leaving current hours.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the return fee could disappear before I know whether a shop will pay for advice. A posted stock-control job with a written wage and a clear plan from the firm would help. I have savings, but I cannot make a hardware shop buy a second meeting.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pays the accountant who has to explain a wrong stock figure to a shop owner. Someone needs a wage for taking responsibility, not just a signature line.

headlineQuote: Someone needs a wage for taking responsibility, not just a signature line.
portrait: Karl, **43**, is an average-skilled mid-level accountant at Pine Ledger with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification.
His **high pay**, eight-month reserve and Amira’s library wage support two school-age children and a mortgage.
He uses AI **occasionally after colleagues** test it, with plenty of other firms nearby if work changes.
He fears **2028 desk cuts** and tests paid stock-loss advice before relying on those client fees.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase return fees before he knows if clients pay for advice.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted stock-control role** with written wages and a firm staffing plan would help.
